Cobb County Superior Court: An Overview

Cobb County Superior Court is a trial court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of cases. The court is located in Marietta, Georgia and serves the citizens of Cobb County. In this article, we will provide a comprehensive overview of Cobb County Superior Court, including its history, jurisdiction, types of cases heard, judges, and court procedures.

History of Cobb County Superior Court

Cobb County Superior Court was established in 1832, the same year Cobb County was created. The court has undergone many changes over the years, including changes to its name and jurisdiction. Today, Cobb County Superior Court is one of the busiest trial courts in the state of Georgia.

Jurisdiction of Cobb County Superior Court

Criminal Jurisdiction

Cobb County Superior Court has jurisdiction over all felony cases in Cobb County, including murder, rape, and drug offenses. The court also has the power to hear and decide misdemeanor cases that have been appealed from the lower courts.

Civil Jurisdiction

Cobb County Superior Court has jurisdiction over civil cases where the amount in controversy exceeds $25,000. These cases may involve contract disputes, personal injury claims, and property disputes.

Juvenile Jurisdiction

Cobb County Superior Court has exclusive jurisdiction over juvenile cases, including delinquency, deprivation, and termination of parental rights.

Types of Cases Heard in Cobb County Superior Court

Criminal Cases

Cobb County Superior Court hears a wide range of criminal cases, including felony and misdemeanor offenses. The court also has jurisdiction over probation revocation hearings and appeals of lower court decisions.

Civil Cases

Cobb County Superior Court hears a variety of civil cases, including contract disputes, personal injury claims, and property disputes. The court also has jurisdiction over appeals of lower court decisions.

Family Law Cases

Cobb County Superior Court hears family law cases, including divorce, child custody, and child support cases.

Juvenile Cases

Cobb County Superior Court has exclusive jurisdiction over juvenile cases, including delinquency, deprivation, and termination of parental rights.

Judges of Cobb County Superior Court

Cobb County Superior Court is comprised of six judges, who are elected by the citizens of Cobb County. The judges serve four-year terms and are responsible for hearing and deciding cases in their assigned divisions.

Court Procedures

Filing a Lawsuit

To file a lawsuit in Cobb County Superior Court, a person must complete a form called a "Complaint" and file it with the court. The Complaint must include a detailed description of the claim being made and the relief being sought.

Serving Papers

After a lawsuit has been filed, the Complaint and other legal documents must be served on the defendant. This is typically done by a process server or the sheriff's office.

Pre-Trial Procedures

Before a case goes to trial, there are several pre-trial procedures that must be completed, including discovery, motion practice, and settlement negotiations.

Trial

If a case proceeds to trial, a judge or a jury will hear the evidence presented by both sides and make a decision based on the facts of the case and the law. In a criminal case, the burden of proof is on the prosecution to prove the defendant's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. In a civil case, the burden of proof is on the plaintiff to prove their case by a preponderance of the evidence.

Appeals

If a party is dissatisfied with the decision of the trial court, they may have the right to appeal the decision to a higher court. Appeals are generally based on errors of law made by the trial court, rather than on a re-examination of the facts of the case.

The docket provides information on the date, time, and location of each hearing, as well as the names of the parties involved in the case.

Conclusion

Cobb County Superior Court is an important institution in the state of Georgia, with the power to hear and decide a wide range of cases. From criminal cases to civil cases, family law cases, and juvenile cases, the court plays a critical role in the administration of justice in Cobb County.
